finding.claim: testBit computes positionInString = length - position, so it reads the bit one position too high (and position 0 reads out of range). inspectTeredo therefore returns wrong coneNat, microsoft.reserved, microsoft.universalLocal and microsoft.groupIndividual values.
finding.source: Any Teredo address (2001::/32) passed to Address6.inspectTeredo(); its flag bits are attacker-controlled input (src/ipv6.ts:954).
finding.sink: testBit() decoding the 16-bit Teredo flag word, results returned as decoded fields (src/ipv6.ts:990-993).

trace.note: flagsBase2 = getBitsBase2(64,80): 16-char string, index 0 is the MSB.
coneNat = testBit(flagsBase2, 15); bit 15 is the C (cone) flag.
Bounds check is position > length, so position == length is not rejected.

positionInString = length - position; should be length - 1 - position. For position 15 this reads index 1 (R bit) instead of index 0 (C bit); for position 0 it reads index 16, which is out of range and always false.

finding.guards_checked: Only the bounds check at common.ts:119, which is itself off by one and does not protect the index calculation. The call-site bit positions (14, 15, 8, 9) match the Microsoft layout CRAAAAUG AAAAAAAA, so the error is in testBit, not the callers. Concrete effects: flags 0x8000 gives coneNat=false (should be true); flags 0x4000 gives coneNat=true (should be false); flags 0x0100 gives universalLocal=true and groupIndividual=false (both reversed). Verified by hand-tracing only; no code was executed. Severity low: decoded data is misreported, and no security decision in this library depends on these fields.
